title: Smooth cohomological duality without a chosen orientation
statement:
Let $A$ be a finite commutative ring and $N\geq1$ an integer with $NA=0$. Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme on which $N$ is invertible, and let $f:X\to S$ be smooth, separated, compactifiable [def-asd-compactifiable], and of pure relative dimension $d\geq0$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Work in the entire ordinary derived categories $D(T_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ of sheaves of modules over the constant ring $A_T$ on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], with inverse image $f^*=f^{-1}$ [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor]. Let $f^\times$ be the right adjoint of the ordinary etale compact-support functor $Rf_!$ [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint, def-amb-etale-compact-support], and put $\omega_f=f^\times A_S$. Then $\omega_f[-2d]$ is isomorphic to a sheaf $L$ in degree zero which is etale locally isomorphic to $A_X$ (a locally constant sheaf of free rank-one $A$-modules). For every $K\in D(S_{\mathrm{et}},A)$, the canonical tensor morphism
$$f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\longrightarrow f^\times K$$
is an isomorphism. Here the canonical morphism is the transpose, under $Rf_!\dashv f^\times$, of the inverse compact-support projection formula followed by $1_K\otimes\epsilon_{A_S}$ and the tensor unit constraint:
$$Rf_!(f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f)\longrightarrow K\otimes_A^LRf_!\omega_f\longrightarrow K\otimes_A^LA_S\longrightarrow K.$$
This statement concerns ordinary etale coefficients, not the unbounded pro-etale category. No orientation of $L$ is chosen.

proof.text: Choose a compactification $f=rj$. For an open immersion, the extension-by-zero stalk is the original stalk in the open and zero outside. Consequently $j_!(j^*P\otimes Q)\cong P\otimes j_!Q$: at a point in the open it is the identity tensor comparison and outside both sides vanish. This holds for total complexes as well. Compute the derived tensor with a K-flat resolution with flat terms of $K$; its inverse image stays K-flat by the ringed-topos tensor-pullback lemma. Since $j_!$ is exact, the termwise comparison computes the derived one. Apply the proper projection formula for $r$ to $j_!M$ to obtain $Rf_!(f^*K\otimes^L M)\cong K\otimes^LRf_!M$, for all unbounded $K,M$. In particular set $M=\omega_f$, compose with the adjunction counit at $A_S$ and the tensor unit constraint, and transpose. This constructs the claimed global map $\alpha_{f,K}$. All schemes in the compactification are Noetherian, since $S$ is Noetherian and the morphisms are finite type.

Because $NA=0$, the coefficient ring is torsion, so [lem-kun-proper-base-change-torsion-ring] applies to every proper rectangle. Together with the unbounded proper/open exchange and compact-support comparison stated in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons], and the extension-by-zero stalk calculation [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-stalks], this gives the canonical proper/open comparison as an isomorphism for every unbounded $A$-module complex.

The refinement, identity, and composition clauses of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] identify all compactification candidates canonically and coherently. Its unbounded composition comparison supplies $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ and the associativity and identity laws, so the compact-support functor is independent of the chosen compactification.

Apply [lem-amb-shriek-tensor-composition] to the canonical projections constructed in step 1. That statement gives the composite projection identity (in the displayed orientation); taking inverses gives the inverse projection orientation used here, and its refinement clause makes the maps independent of compactification. This supplies the tensor compatibility needed when transposing through composite adjunctions.

proof.text: For composable $X\xrightarrow{a}Y\xrightarrow{b}Z$ among the maps used below, the bases are qcqs because they are Noetherian. Nagata and [prop-nagata-compactification-category] give compactifications and common/equalizing refinements. The proper/open tower specified in [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons] therefore applies; its normalization is exactly the one used in steps 3 and 4.

proof.text:
At each point of $X$, the smooth local normal form supplies affine opens $U\subset X$, $V\subset S$ and an etale map $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$. The dimension in this form is the given $d$: the etale map has zero-dimensional relative fibres, and [sbc-lem-affine-space-smooth] says that projection from affine space has relative dimension equal to its number of coordinates; apply [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence] to the etale map and that projection. At the chosen point the resulting dimension equals $d$, so the chart integer is $d$. Compose the etale map with the open immersion $\mathbf A^d_V\subset\mathbf A^d_S$ to obtain a separated finite-type etale $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$ with $fu=p_de$, where $u:U\hookrightarrow X$. Thus the original base $S$ is retained. The maps $u,e,p_d,fu$ are compactifiable by Nagata, applied to their separated finite-type maps and qcqs Noetherian bases. Use the ordinary-etale projective-line adjunction [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction], restrict by the exact open extension adjunction to affine lines, and iterate using steps 3–5. This supplies $Rp_{d!}\dashv p_d^*(d)[2d]$ with its twist explicitly $A(1)=\mu_N\otimes_{\mathbf Z/N}A$ on the ordinary etale site. In particular it makes no identification with def-coefficient-twists-detailed. Etale adjoint locality for $u$ and $e$ then identifies
$$u^*f^\times K\cong (fu)^\times K\cong e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d],\qquad u^*\omega_f\cong A_U(d)[2d].$$
Here the finite etale twist is defined by the new ordinary projective-line input, with the same annihilator $N$ as the twist-line lemma. The affine iteration uses pullback of roots of unity and the tensor identity $A(1)^{\otimes d}=A(d)$, not an adic comparison. Step 7 below fixes the counit of that iterated adjunction. The identification is the unique comparison of right adjoints through their Hom bijections.

source.place: Tag 054L, lemma-smooth-etale-over-affine-space; adjunction calculation follows the blueprint second paragraph

proof.text:
Fix the normalization of the affine-space adjunction, rather than merely an abstract isomorphism of its right adjoint. On $\mathbf P^1_S$, the adjunction counit is, by [lem-asd-ordinary-finite-p1-adjunction] for our arbitrary finite $A$,
$$Rq_*q^*K(1)[2]\cong K\otimes^LRq_*A(1)[2]\xrightarrow{1\otimes t_q}K.$$
For $j:\mathbf A^1_S\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^1_S$, the right adjoint of $Rq_*j_!$ is $j^*q^*(1)[2]$. Its counit is $Rq_*$ of the counit $j_!j^*\to\mathrm{id}$ followed by the displayed counit. The open-immersion tensor comparison from step 1 sends this composite to $1_K$ tensored with its value at $A_S$. Use the unbounded composition comparison of step 3 and its tensor compatibility from step 4. Iterating the affine-line factorization of $p_d$ gives the same assertion for $p_d$: the composite counit is obtained by successively applying the $d$ line counits. For $d=0$ it is the identity. Tensor reassociation sends $x\otimes m_1\otimes\cdots\otimes m_d$ to the same tensor at each stage, so its transpose is exactly the canonical isomorphism $p_d^*K\otimes^LA(d)[2d]\cong p_d^*K(d)[2d]$.

For each separated finite-type etale chart map $v=u$ or $e$, [lem-asd-etale-sum-extension-tensor] gives the unbounded tensor comparison for sum extension and its compatibility with the fold counit. The comparison is the one used by the compactification projection in [lem-pur-etale-support-map-compatibility](2), so the tensor projection can be moved through the counit in both chart factorizations.

source.place: Proof paragraph 3: etale sum-extension tensor and counit calculation

proof.text: Apply [lem-asd-tensor-mate-etale-precomp] to $f$ and $u:U\hookrightarrow X$. With $h=fu$, its displayed equality identifies $u^*\alpha_{f,K}$ with the canonical tensor mate $\alpha_{h,K}$ after the locality identifications, including $u^*\omega_f\cong\omega_h$ and the composite counit.

Apply [lem-asd-tensor-mate-etale-precomp] again, now with $f=p_d$ and $u=e$. The maps $p_d,e,h=p_de$ satisfy its compactifiability and Noetherian hypotheses by step 6. Its same equality identifies $e^*\alpha_{p_d,K}$ with $\alpha_{h,K}$, inserting the isomorphisms $e^*p_d^\times B\cong h^\times B$ at $B=K,A_S$. By step 7 the affine-space mate is the tensor reassociation isomorphism; exact inverse image and the canonical tensor-pullback isomorphism preserve it. Thus $\alpha_{h,K}$ is invertible.

The affine charts of step 6 cover $X$. Steps 9–10 show that the pullback of the globally constructed canonical map is invertible on every such chart, with the same original base $S$. These are the local isomorphisms used in the following stalk test.

Inverse image on etale module sheaves is exact, so it commutes with cohomology. The charts of step 6 cover $X$, and step 11 therefore makes every geometric stalk of every cohomology map $\mathcal H^i(\alpha_{f,K})$ an isomorphism. Apply the geometric-stalk criterion to each underlying abelian cohomology sheaf. Every $\mathcal H^i(\alpha_{f,K})$ is an isomorphism; equivalently its cone is acyclic, so $\alpha_{f,K}$ is an isomorphism in the ordinary derived category. This uses no bounded-below hypothesis and applies the sheaf-level criterion only to sheaves.

The local model $u^*\omega_f\cong A_U(d)[2d]$ and the twist-line lemma give $\mathcal H^i(\omega_f)=0$ for $i\ne-2d$: exact inverse image and the sheaf-stalk criterion detect this vanishing. Put $L=\mathcal H^{-2d}(\omega_f)$. It is locally isomorphic to $A_U(d)$, and refining the chart by a twist trivialization makes it isomorphic to $A$, which is precisely the stated local rank-one condition. To identify the complex globally, take a representative $C$ of $\omega_f$ and let $q=-2d$. The good truncation $\tau_{\le q}C\to C$ is a quasi-isomorphism because cohomology above $q$ vanishes. The projection $\tau_{\le q}C\to L[-q]$ is a quasi-isomorphism because its kernel is acyclic (cohomology below $q$ vanishes and its degree-$q$ cycles equal its boundaries). These two quasi-isomorphisms give $\omega_f\cong L[2d]$. No local choices of a primitive root or of a basis of $L$ are glued into an orientation.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be smooth, separated, compactifiable,
and of pure relative dimension $d$, with Noetherian base.
Put $\omega_f=f^\times A_S$, using the ambient right
adjoint. Then $\omega_f[-2d]$ is a locally constant
sheaf of free rank-one $A$-modules. For every complex
$K$ on $S$, the canonical tensor morphism is an
isomorphism

$$
f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f\xrightarrow{\sim}f^\times K.
$$

proof.text:
Construct the tensor morphism by transposing

$$
Rf_!(f^*K\otimes_A^L\omega_f)
\cong K\otimes_A^LRf_!\omega_f
\longrightarrow K\otimes_A^LA_S=K
$$

under [thm-amb-etale-exceptional-adjoint].
The displayed projection formula follows from
[lem-amb-proper-coproducts-projection] on a compactification:
extension by zero commutes with tensoring a pulled-back
complex, as its stalk is either that complex or zero.

By [sbc-thm-etale-local-normal-form], every point of
$X$ has an etale neighbourhood $u:U\to X$ such
that $fu=p_de$, where $e:U\to\mathbf A^d_S$
is etale (one may restrict the base to an open neighbourhood).
The adjunctions in
[lem-amb-etale-adjoint-locality], [cor-amb-affine-space-adjunction]
identify

$$
u^*f^\times K\cong e^*p_d^*K(d)[2d],\qquad
u^*\omega_f\cong A_U(d)[2d].
$$

By its definition as the transpose of the projection formula
and counit, the tensor map restricts under these identifications
to the canonical reassociation
$(fu)^*K\otimes_A^LA_U(d)[2d]\cong(fu)^*K(d)[2d]$.
To check this assertion, transpose on $U$: both maps
become the projection formula followed by the composite of
the etale counit with the $d$ affine-line counits. The
uniqueness in the adjunction bijection therefore identifies
them. In particular it is an isomorphism locally on $X$,
hence globally by
[lemma-weil-pbc-geometric-stalk-conservative].

The same local calculation shows that all cohomology sheaves
of $\omega_f$ except $\mathcal H^{-2d}$ vanish,
and that $\mathcal H^{-2d}(\omega_f)$ is etale locally
free of rank one. The canonical truncation isomorphism
$\omega_f\cong\mathcal H^{-2d}(\omega_f)[2d]$
gives the stated conclusion. No complexes or morphisms were
glued in a derived category: the adjoint and tensor morphism
were constructed globally, and geometric stalks only tested
their properties.
